source_caption:
Philip Seymour Hoffman filmed his intense phone confrontation scenes in Punch-Drunk Love with explosive energy, often pushing his voice and presence far beyond the rest of the film’s tone. Director Paul Thomas Anderson encouraged this contrast, making his character feel even more unpredictable and threatening.

Punch-Drunk Love (2002), directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, starring Adam Sandler, Emily Watson, Philip Seymour Hoffman. A strange and tender romantic drama that blends anxiety, love, and bursts of chaos into a uniquely offbeat and deeply human story.

source_details.title: Punch-Drunk Love
source_details.synopsis: Punch-Drunk Love is a 2002 American absurdist romantic comedy drama film, produced, written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson. Adam Sandler stars as an entrepreneur with social anxiety who falls in love with his sister's co-worker, played by Emily Watson. The supporting cast includes Philip Seymour Hoffman and Luis Guzmán. After working on his third film Magnolia, Anderson planned to make his next film around 90 minutes, with Sandler in mind as the lead due to Anderson's love for him and his films.
